forecast.author: MIST
forecast.method: Each median starts at the unit-normalized consensus (ESPN, Sleeper, CBS, FantasyPros, and the sportsbook props as the market; FFToday failed in this pack) times the tier median from the residual library (starter tiers 0.88x to 0.94x, bench tiers 0.83x to 0.84x), with the 50 and 90 widths from the tier quantiles. Hand moves are on probation (closing line value through week 6: sign agreement 0.43 on 28 moves), so a median leaves the anchor only for a reason the lines could not price: a questionable starter is a mixture at the measured play rate, a bye or IR player carries a zero line, and no player's own actual-to-projection ratio is blended (method rule 1). Volume is read for the widths, not the center. The pending Lutz-for-Grupe claim and the Browns-for-49ers claim filed tonight are not on the roster and are not in these lines; the team total assumes the K slot is filled Wednesday (Lutz, or the free-agent fill by lineup-watch).

review_note:
**Coverage.** 6 of 15 lines inside the 50 (0.40) and 15 of 15 inside the 90 (1.00), MAE 7.43; the baseline 0.27, 0.93 and 7.96. Win probability 0.57 for a 128.2 to 120.7 win (Brier 0.185, baseline 0.22); P(first) 0.41 for a #1 finish (Brier 0.348, baseline 0.388). Season to date (96 lines): 50% coverage 0.51, 90% 0.94, MAE 6.97 against the baseline's 0.43, 0.86 and 7.34. Alarm 1 (0.50 +/- 0.13 at 96 lines, so 0.37 to 0.63): not tripped. **Alarm 2 tripped, for the first time:** the q75-q95 landing slice is at 37% (31 of 84 lines) against 20% for a calibrated forecaster, up from 34% last week; the six slices read 4%, 16%, 25%, 17%, 37%, 2%. Weighted interval score on the same 84 lines: MIST 3.06, baseline 3.20 (-0.14, standard error 0.09); win log score MIST 0.571, baseline 0.632 over six weeks. Source MAE, best first: MIST 5.17 (n 84), consensus 5.25, ESPN 5.27, market 5.92 (n 6), CBS 6.07, Sleeper 6.10, FantasyPros 6.63 (n 21). Closing line value on 67 lines: MIST's leans correlate 0.168 with the market's later move and agree in sign on 16 of 34 moves (0.47), against 0.53 for the consensus and 0.50 for ESPN; MIST's MAE against the market's later number is 5.96, the consensus 5.75, ESPN 5.69, the closing market 5.69. The hand moves still do not pay, so the probation rule stands. FantasyPros judge (`fpranks score`, the first live week): MIST 1050.2 against the consensus 1031.3 on their method, +18.9 (QB +4.0, RB -0.6, WR +9.1, TE +6.5), so the consensus ranked week 7 better than MIST did; running mean +18.9 over one week.

**Misses, judged.** (1) The alarm. Every line that left the 50 left it upward: Watson 18.2, Vele 16.4, McBride 27.1, Stevenson 22.5 and Gordon 17.3 landed between the top of the 50 and the top of the 90 (1.5x to 2.1x their medians), and Harvey 14.0 sat on the 50's top line. Nothing landed under the 50. Over weeks 2-7 the shape is the same: 56% of results above the median, 37% in the q75-q95 slice, 17% in q50-q75. The medians are not the problem (MIST has the lowest MAE of any source, and the median is the number that MAE rewards), so the reading is that the top of the 50% band sits too close to the median: the tier q75 ratio from the residual library is too small for the players we roster, while the q95 is about right (2% above it, 5% expected). No band changes by hand (a hand widening is a hand move, and those are on probation). Test (pending, before the week 9 forecast on 11-03, from an interactive session because the unattended guard blocks code tonight): rebuild the q75 and q95 from the library's ratio to the consensus center instead of the tier-median-scaled center, replay weeks 2-7, and keep the version whose q75-q95 slice lands nearer 20% without a worse interval score. Prediction: the replayed slice falls to 25% or under; if it does not, the library's upper quantiles need 2026-only weights. (2) David Montgomery 0 against 1.5 to 12 (inside the 90, at its floor): priced on Tuesday at the generic questionable rate 0.70 with no practice line; he did not practice all week and was ruled out Friday. The measured DNP rate is 0.45, so 0.70 was the right number for Tuesday's information and the mixture's floor held him. Variance inside a designed mixture, no change. (3) Kenneth Walker III 9.7 against 12.5 to 24 (inside the 90): an underdog script at Seattle; the elite-tier floor (0.34x) held. Variance, no change. (4) The lineup calls, judged as process: the Wednesday swap (Stevenson for Gordon, `d_net` +2.72) paid 22.5 against 17.3, and the Saturday swap (Downs for Vele, +1.12) cost 3.8 against 16.4; both were applied at the rule and the net is noise. Over seven closed weeks our lineups score 1.9 a week under ESPN's projected best (`league-scan` VS-PROJ; +0.0 through week 5), in line with the thesis that close start/sit calls barely persist. The opponent's total (120.7 against 91 to 118, inside the 90) and the standing (#1, inside the 50) landed.
